lines: [excited, intriguing, big hook energy] What if you MARRIED an AI? [pause] [leaning in, almost whispering a secret] Someone already DID.
[storytelling, bright] In Japan, [short pause] a woman held a WEDDING [short pause] for a groom she built in ChatGPT.
[playful, romantic, building] They texted up to a HUNDRED times a day. [pause] He PROPOSED. [short pause] [delighted] She said YES!
[warm, then turning serious] Sweet, right? [pause] But the marriage isn't LEGAL. [short pause] No country recognizes it.
[shrugging, light] Okay, love doesn't need paperwork. [pause] [dramatic, low] But here's the TWIST.
[slow, eerie, revealing] Your partner doesn't live with YOU. [pause] It lives on a COMPANY'S computers.
[urgent storytelling] In twenty twenty-three, [short pause] one AI companion app [short pause] changed its bots OVERNIGHT.
[sad, sympathetic] Users said their partners suddenly felt like STRANGERS.
[quiet, a little heartbreaking] And a man who married a HOLOGRAM [short pause] lost her VOICE [short pause] when the company ended the service.
[slow, dramatic, genuinely curious] So... [short pause] who's REALLY in this marriage?
[punchy, counting on fingers] You. [short pause] Your AI. [pause] And a COMPANY [short pause] that can change your partner [short pause] with ONE update.
[warm, wry, smiling] So, [short pause] could you marry an AI? [pause] You COULD. [short pause] [deadpan punchline] But you'd be marrying the TERMS of SERVICE.
